title: Phishing attacks - bank liability under RBI guidelines
p1:
Lost money to a phishing scam? Your bank may be responsible for the loss, even if the transaction happened through your own account.

But there is one crucial detail most people overlook: how quickly you report the fraud can determine whether you get your money back.
p2:
Many people assume that once they share an OTP or click a fake banking link, the bank has no responsibility.

That is not always true.

Under RBI guidelines, customers can have zero liability for unauthorized electronic transactions if the fraud resulted from the bank's negligence or a system deficiency. Even where a third-party breach occurs, prompt reporting can protect customers from financial liability.
p3:
Here is the practical rule:

If an unauthorized transaction occurs, report it to your bank immediately and through its official channels. Under RBI rules, reporting within three working days of receiving the bank's transaction communication can qualify you for zero liability in certain third-party breach cases.

If you shared confidential credentials through negligence, you may bear the loss until you report it. Transactions occurring after reporting are generally the bank's responsibility.

Also, banks are required to provide a shadow reversal within 10 working days of notification in qualifying cases.
conclusion: If someone tricks you into revealing an OTP through a fake banking website, should the bank automatically escape liability? What do you think?
